scope: Staged closed-registry contracts-v1 generator adapter under the development-trusted-host profile. Not product integration approval, not full M1 completion, not TS2/Rust3/control/report protocol coverage, not an inventory successor or design-lock change. The eight-output02 algorithm review is not duplicated.
verdictSummary: Pins, drift, output ownership, TS package snapshotting, tool substitution refusal and write-failure safety hold under independent mutation. Four small corrections are required before this meets the boundary it claims: (1) generation accepts unsupported schema keywords, including unregistered remote refs, and writes outputs; (2) output roles are not bound to the accepted row contract; (3) the verifier runs ambient Python code without -I, and -O removes a projection guard; (4) the dependency guard silently admits undeclared dev-dependencies. This is not hermetic and does not claim to be: native libraries and rustfmt are verified and then loaded from host paths, the Python interpreter/stdlib is mostly unpinned, the entrypoint verifies itself, and nothing binds the generator binary to its pinned source.

inputsVerifiedBeforeUse.sources: All 28 registry sources are byte-identical to the architecture sources named in schemas/source-map.json; majors and namespace/module owners agree with options.json.

confirmedProperties: Baseline drift check on a review-owned copy: exit 0, 8 outputs, changed [] (4.6 s).
Generation runs no Cargo, npm or pnpm subprocess. Children are the snapshot generator, snapshot node and verified rustfmt, with env {PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, HOME=empty temp, LANG/LC_ALL=C, TZ=UTC}.

Traced Node module resolution under the minimal env: only snapshot generate-ts.cjs, render-types.cjs, node_modules/typescript/lib/typescript.js and builtins (perf_hooks, fs, path, os, crypto). Nothing resolves outside the copied tooling snapshot.
Source, options, closure and pinned tool-file byte changes without rebinding are refused (M01, M04, M22).
Consistently rebound source/owner-module/type-name substitutions are refused by drift (M02, M05, M06). After an explicit --write, a recheck is clean (M02c).
Undeclared outputs (extra .rs, hidden file, nested dir), dropped or extra output rows, symlinked output files and symlinked generated dirs are all refused before any write (M13-M17).
Drift in one file refuses. --write replaces only the drifted or missing file, and the recheck is clean (M18, M19).
Tampered generator bytes, a relative tool path and a different Python interpreter are refused (M20). rustfmt with identical bytes at a relocated path fails at load and refuses without writes (M21).
A TS stage failure after the Rust stage with a pending --write leaves the tree unchanged (M24).
TS package tamper, an extra file, a nested symlink, a package or node_modules symlinked outside the tooling workspace (identical bytes) are all refused (M25a-e).
An interrupted multi-file --write leaves no temp files, and the next drift check detects the remaining file (W1). This matches the documented non-atomic contract.
Subject tools/tests/test_generation.py: 12 tests OK on the review copy.

Dependency guard refuses an added feature, undeclared normal/build/optional-default/path dependencies, a root build script, an extra bin target, a policy checksum mismatch and a missing feature row (D01, D02, D04, D05b, D07-D12).

boundaryAssessment.requirement: Closed registry source/recipe/output row contract (build plan section 'Closed generation registry')
boundaryAssessment.detail: Closed fields, duplicate-key and float refusal, raw digests, ID/dialect, sorted unique lists, canonical paths and output consumer directories are enforced. Roles are not bound to the accepted per-path contract (R2). The semantic owner is an unchecked free string (A4).

boundaryAssessment.requirement: All transitive schema references resolve within registered inputs; no implicit remote references
boundaryAssessment.detail: Refs are resolved only under the keywords prepare.py traverses. Unsupported subschema keywords pass through, and generation writes outputs embedding unregistered refs (R1).

boundaryAssessment.requirement: Regenerate into a fresh temporary tree and compare every declared byte; explicit membership only
Hermetic generator closure identified by recipe
boundaryAssessment.detail: The development-trusted-host profile is declared honestly, but see A1 and A2. Do not describe this as hermetic.

boundaryAssessment.requirement: Isolated generation lane; tool dependencies separate from pure contracts runtime
boundaryAssessment.detail: tools/contracts is excluded from the root Cargo workspace and has its own Cargo.lock and pnpm lock. There is no package-manager subprocess at generation. The provisioning/install lane itself is not demonstrated (A10).

requiredFindings.title: Generation accepts unsupported schema keywords, including unregistered remote references
requiredFindings.evidence: M03a-d: a consistently rebound dispatch.v1 source adding prefixItems:[{$ref:'https://unregistered.invalid/x.json'}], dependentSchemas{$ref}, $dynamicRef or unevaluatedProperties{$ref} was accepted with --write (exit 0), and all 8 outputs were rewritten. report.ts embeds the unregistered URLs. The Rust and provider carriers silently ignore the keyword. The TS runtime refuses unknown keywords only lazily, in checkEntryPoints at validate time (runtime/schema.ts:76, :111).
requiredFindings.correction: In prepare.flatten.convert, refuse any schema-object key outside the closed keyword set runtime/schema.ts already selects (known plus annotations). Share one list rather than a second copy, or add a test asserting the two are equal. Also refuse unknown keys in non-selected positions reached by a selected ref. Add a test_generation case with a remote $ref under prefixItems.

requiredFindings.title: Output roles are unconstrained relative to the accepted row contract
requiredFindings.evidence: M09: registry rows with mod.rs roles [carrier, shape-validator] and report.ts roles [module-index] were accepted with --write. The build plan requires mod.rs to be module-index and report.ts to be carrier+shape-validator; the Rust files are inert carriers.
requiredFindings.correction: For contracts-v1, require exact roles per path: generated/mod.rs is [module-index]; other generated/*.rs are [carrier]; apps/report/.../report.ts is [carrier, shape-validator]; providers/typescript/.../protocol.ts is [carrier]. Refuse otherwise and add a mutation test.

requiredFindings.title: Verifier does not enforce interpreter isolation; -O removes a projection guard
requiredFindings.evidence: M28: without -I and with PYTHONPATH=sitecustomize, the injected code ran inside the verifier, and generation still reported success. The python pin checks only the 52 KB launcher. O1: under -O, prepare.rust silently widens an unselected pattern map into additionalProperties {} (AssertionError without -O). The assert error is also outside main's caught exception types.
requiredFindings.correction: At generate() entry, refuse unless sys.flags.isolated and not sys.flags.optimize (and dont_write_bytecode, if intended). Replace the two asserts in prepare.rust with ValueError. Add tests for both.

requiredFindings.title: Dependency guard silently admits undeclared dev-dependencies
requiredFindings.evidence: D03: adding [dev-dependencies] sha2-const-stable to crates/contracts passes with dependencyCount 11. Build plan enforcement 1 requires dev-only exceptions to be recorded explicitly.
requiredFindings.correction: Add an explicit devDependencies list (currently empty) to dependency-policy.json. Refuse subject-package dev edges not in it and report them in the result. Add negative tests for check() with small synthetic metadata (D02, D03, D05, D07) so the guard is exercised without cargo.

advisories.title: Ambient effects that keep this from being hermetic
advisories.detail: (a) rustfmt runs from its verified original path, and the four Homebrew dylibs are hashed and then loaded later by the OS loader (TOCTOU). The pins read /opt/homebrew/opt/* alias paths while the loader resolves @loader_path/../lib under Cellar; the paths coincide today only through Homebrew symlinks. (b) The nativeLibraries list is self-declared: N1 dropped the libz3 pin, rebound, and --write was accepted. Completeness is not derived from the loader closure. (c) The Python framework dylib and stdlib are unpinned. (d) generate_contracts.py verifies itself, so S1 (an edited entrypoint skipping its pins) accepted a tampered render-types.cjs. Authority must come from an independently verified entrypoint, not the closure. (e) There is no filesystem or network confinement of the pinned executables; TMPDIR is inherited. Simplest reduction: format in-process with prettyplease inside the generator, which removes rustfmt and about 280 MB of native libraries (requires re-baselining outputs).

advisories.title: No binary/source join for the generator
advisories.detail: The closure pins tools/contracts/src/*.rs and Cargo.lock and, separately, the generator executable hash, but nothing proves one was built from the other. The candidate's target/debug dep-info names the candidate sources, whose current bytes match the pins, but that is adjacency, not provenance. The binary is a debug build. Record the build identity (cargo/rustc version, lock, profile, target, flags, remap-path-prefix), or rebuild independently and compare, before selecting the recipe.

advisories.title: Superseded exclusions are self-declared
advisories.detail: M07: removing HelloV3 from deniedRefs and adding it as an entry point, rebound, was accepted with --write. Add a test binding deniedRefs to the accepted metadata-v2 superseded set so this change cannot pass as a routine options diff.

advisories.title: Registry, options and source-map agreement is not mechanical
advisories.detail: M08: a consistent declaredMajor 7 and semanticValidatorOwner '../../outside/owner' in both registry and options was accepted. schemas/source-map.json is read by no tool or test, even though it currently agrees. Validate the owner as a canonical repository path and cross-check majors, owners and architecture digests against source-map.json in a test.

advisories.title: Source paths are unrestricted
advisories.detail: M10: a source relocated to tools/zz-moved/dispatch.json was accepted. Restrict sourcePath to schemas/sources/.

advisories.title: Dependency guard coverage limits
advisories.detail: D05: a cfg(windows) dependency is invisible to a darwin --target run. Declare the supported target set in the policy and check each. D13: root-crate features are unchecked. Build scripts of the selected dependencies are accepted without a recorded effect review in policy.

advisories.title: Machine-readable output mixes child output with the summary
advisories.detail: Generator and node stdout ('generated six Rust files' and the export JSON) precede the final summary. Capture child stdout, or print the summary to a distinct stream.

advisories.title: Tests do not exercise generate() refusal paths
advisories.detail: test_generation.py covers registry and options only. Add stub-executable tests for closure, tool and TS-package mismatch, undeclared output, drift and write-failure refusal; these need no real generator. test_pattern_projection_refuses_unknown_map uses an empty regex.

advisories.title: Provisioning lane unverified against the lock
advisories.detail: The candidate's node_modules/.pnpm holds packages beyond pnpm-lock.yaml, such as @apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser. They are harmless here because only the verified typescript tree is copied, but an explicit offline install recipe matching the lock is still undemonstrated.

advisories.title: Single-recipe hard coding
advisories.detail: contracts-v1 only, exactly 8 outputs and 5 fixed modules in main.rs. This is acceptable for the staged candidate, but multi-recipe regeneration into one tree remains open.

advisories.title: Toolchain selection
advisories.detail: No rustup: rust-toolchain.toml does not select the toolchain on this host (Homebrew cargo/rustfmt 1.95.0). Toolchain identity is established only by hash.

remainingBeforeHermeticSelectedRecipeOrP: Remove or snapshot the native tool closure (A1a/b), preferably with in-process formatting. Otherwise derive the library set from the loader and verify realpaths at exec.
Establish the generator binary provenance join (A2).
Define the trusted entrypoint and interpreter identity outside the closure the entrypoint verifies (A1c/d).
Run under effect confinement (no network, read-only inputs, write-only temp) if 'hermetic' is to be claimed.
Demonstrate the offline provisioning lane for the Rust generator and TS package from locks (A9).
Mechanically bind registry, options, source-map and metadata-v2 superseded selections (A3, A4).

Close the protocol coverage obligations listed in options.openObligations (TS2, Rust3, control, report envelope4) and the separately pending inventory successor/design-lock decisions; this review infers no authority from current lock3.
